title: When disconnecting secondary screen that has the system's only panel, the new primary screen has no panel
line: When you unplug a screen that has your only panels, those panels move to the remaining screen and go back when you plug it in again.
explanation: When a screen is unplugged, plasmashell hides the panels assigned to it and keeps them waiting for that screen index to come back. If the primary screen had no panels of its own, nothing was left on screen, even after restarting plasmashell. Now, on unplug, if no panel is assigned to the primary screen, the removed screen's panels are moved there and their old screen is remembered in the containment config (screenBeforeRemoval); when that screen index is added again they move back. Moving a panel by hand (Manage Desktops and Panels, scripting) clears the remembered screen.

commits.message:
shell: don't leave the primary screen without panels on unplug

When a screen with panels was disconnected and the primary screen had no
panels of its own, those panels were hidden and nothing was left. Move
them to the primary screen instead, and back once that screen returns.

BUG: 480634

media.caption: Pure master: the only panel was on the secondary screen; after unplugging it the primary screen has no panel (sweep tester's shot)
With the fix: same steps, the panel now shows on the remaining primary screen

reviews.text: Valid direction that cleanly implements the proposed fallback-to-primary-and-restore-on-replug design in ShellCorona, and the verification demonstrates the 2-screen unplug/replug and plasmashell-restart flows. Before merging, a few edge cases in ShellCorona::handleScreenRemoved() and the screenAdded handler need tightening around types, undo-deleted panels, and removing a non-last screen.
changes: Use int instead of uint for removedScreen (m_screenPool->screenOrder().size() - 1) to match cont->screen()'s int return type and avoid unsigned underflow (where 0 - 1 wraps to UINT_MAX and matches (uint)-1) if screenOrder() is ever empty.

Ignore panels pending undo-deletion (!cont->destroyed()) in both handleScreenRemoved() and the screenAdded handler, so a recently deleted panel on screen 0 does not block moving the removed screen's panels and a deleted panel is not moved or rewritten.

Avoid calling panelView->setScreenToFollow() targeting the dying QScreen when a non-last screen (e.g. screen 0 when closing a laptop lid) is removed while screen 1 holds the only panel: in handleScreenRemoved(), m_screenPool->screenForId(0) still points to the removed screen before handleScreenOrderChanged() updates screenOrder().
